metaDescription: Oreck bagged upright vacuums compared by weight, brush speed, HEPA media and commercial or home build, so you pick the right nine-pound upright.
expertTake: The Oreck HEPA upright is the best pick for a home because it pairs the brand's light frame with HEPA media and a two-speed brush roll. The Oreck Commercial XL is the value pick for a workhorse that weighs only about nine pounds. Skip the family for thick wall-to-wall carpet in a large house; these light machines trade deep agitation for easy carrying.
introParagraphs: This maker built its reputation on a very light bagged upright, and every machine in the current range follows the same formula: a thin plastic body, a bag, a fast brush roll and a weight that a person can carry with one hand.

The differences are in the details: whether the machine is sold as a home or commercial model, whether it carries a HEPA filter, and how the brush roll is controlled. Because all the machines are bagged and light, the questions are about filtration, brush speed and how much abuse the thin frame will tolerate.

products.name: Oreck HEPA upright, bagged, HEPA media, two-speed roll

specList.label: Filtration
specList.value: HEPA media filtration, locks in debris

specList.label: Capacity
specList.value: Holds up to 4X more than a standard bagless

products.description:
This is the Oreck for a home. A bag collects the dirt and HEPA media filtration locks in debris, which the maker says traps fine particles that would otherwise pass through a basic filter. A two-speed controllable brush roll lets you slow the roll for hardwood, tile and rugs and speed it up for carpet, a flexibility that the commercial models lack.

The bag holds, the maker says, up to four times more debris than a typical bagless cup, which means fewer interruptions and less handling of the dust. Next to the Commercial XL it adds HEPA and the roll control, so it is better in a home with allergies, while the XL is the tougher machine.

The bag is the part to manage: change it at about two thirds full, check that it seats flat and keep spares with the vacuum. Replace the HEPA media on the maker's schedule, because a loaded filter strains the motor. The belt-driven roll needs a new belt every six to twelve months, and the thin plastic body is fragile if dropped, so carry it by the handle and park it standing, and avoid pulling it backward by the cord, which is the way most of these machines lose a plug. A practical habit with a light machine is to work in slow, overlapping strokes rather than fast ones, because the roll does the agitating and a hurried pass skips the pile, and to stop every few rooms to feel the bag, since a half-empty bag that feels heavy is usually a sign of fine dust packing into the fabric.
products.bestFor: Homes with allergies that want a light bagged machine.
pros: Two-speed brush roll for floor types
Bag holds far more than a typical cup
cons: Thin frame is fragile if dropped
Belt-driven roll needs a belt change

products.name: Oreck Commercial XL bagged upright, 9 lb, auto height
products.description:
The XL is the best-known Oreck: a commercial machine that weighs about nine pounds and adjusts its own height, so it handles carpet and hard floor without a dial. A high-speed brush roll provides the agitation, and a bag collects the dirt.

It is sold as a commercial model, which here means a simpler, tougher build than a home version, though still light. Compared with the HEPA upright it lacks HEPA media and roll control, but it is the proven workhorse.

Change the bag at two thirds full, replace the belt on schedule and check the brush for thread. Because the height adjusts itself, you do not have a setting to forget, but the mechanism can clog with lint, so tilt the machine back and clear the base plate every month. Because the machine is so light, it is easy to run it over a cord or a loose rug corner, so make a quick sweep of the room first and lift stray cables out of the way, since a cord wound around the roll can snap the belt in a second and leave a burning smell. In a small office it is worth buying two spare belts, a few bags and a spare filter together so that a repair never takes the machine out of service for more than a few minutes.
products.bestFor: Busy homes and small offices that want a light, simple machine.
cons: Thin body is not very rugged

products.name: Oreck Commercial upright, LEED compliant, 9 lb, bagged
products.description:
The LEED-compliant version is built for offices that follow green building standards, where the vacuum's filtration and emissions are part of the building specification. It keeps the nine pound weight, the bag and the commercial build of the XL.

The point of buying this one is the compliance, not a performance difference, so if you are not in a certified building, the XL gives the same machine for the same job. The Microsweep roll helps on hard floors.

Swap the bag once it is two thirds full, check the belt and keep the filter clean. Ask the seller to confirm the compliance documents before you rely on them for a project, and keep a copy with the building file, because the compliance applies to a specific configuration and a replaced filter or bag of a different type can change the picture. Beyond that, treat it as any light commercial upright: store it standing, wind the cord loosely and avoid using it on wet floors, damp carpet or fine construction dust, which will shorten the life of the thin motor and clog the filter within a single shift.
products.bestFor: Offices that need a LEED-compliant vacuum.
cons: Compliance does not change cleaning performance

products.name: Oreck Commercial Professional upright, bagged, 9 lb
products.description:
The Professional is another of the nine pound commercial uprights, and the listing positions it for carpets and hard floors in offices and homes. It carries the family's light bagged formula without extras.

Next to the XL it is a close sibling, with the same weight and approach, so the choice between them often comes down to which is in stock. It is a plain machine for a plain job.

Retire the bag at two thirds full, check the belt and keep spare bags in the closet. A very light machine tips easily, so park it standing against a wall. If you inherit one with a worn belt, you will often see the symptom before you see the cause: the roll stops turning, the machine pushes dirt around and a faint smell of rubber appears, and the fix is a two-minute belt change with a coin or a screwdriver. Replace the filter at the same time, wash any removable parts that the manual allows and let them dry completely, which turns a tired machine into one that behaves like new.
products.bestFor: Offices and homes that want a basic light commercial upright.

products.name: Oreck Commercial Professional with high-speed double helix roll
products.description:
The double helix brush roll is the distinguishing feature of this Professional: a high-speed roll with a spiral pattern designed to lift dirt from carpet and sweep hard floors. It keeps the nine pound weight and the bag.

Compared with the XL it carries a different roll design and a similar frame, so it is aimed at users who want agitation on carpet. The spiral roll is a manufacturer feature, so treat the pickup claim as the maker's.

Pick thread off the roll, replace the belt on schedule and change the bag early. A high-speed roll is hard on a belt, so keep spares, and fit the new belt around the motor shaft first and then the roll, with the flat side facing the same way the old one did, because a belt fitted twisted tears itself apart within minutes. A spiral roll can also pull thread and hair into the center of the spiral, so cut it free along the grooves with a seam ripper rather than pulling, which keeps the roll's pattern intact and lets it keep sweeping hard floors cleanly.
products.bestFor: Carpet-heavy offices that want a light machine with a spiral roll.
cons: High-speed roll is hard on belts

buyingCriteria.explanation: Every Oreck here weighs about nine pounds, which is the brand's selling point. A light frame means thin plastic, so the machine does not tolerate being dropped or used as a ladder. Carry it by the handle and treat it as a light tool, and recognize that the low weight is also the reason these machines skim over thick pile, so they are best matched to low and medium carpet, hard floors and the rental or office work that the brand was designed around.

All the models use disposable bags, which contain dust but cost money and must be changed before they pack. The HEPA upright's bag holds up to four times more than a typical bagless cup. Keep spare bags with the vacuum, and make sure you buy the style that fits the exact model, since a bag of the wrong shape leaves gaps at the intake where dust bypasses the bag and coats the motor, which is the opposite of what a bagged machine is supposed to do.

Only the Oreck HEPA upright lists HEPA media filtration. For allergies, it is the one to choose. The commercial models use a standard filter, which keeps coarse dust out of the motor but does not capture the finest particles, so a household with asthma or a pet allergy should treat the HEPA model as the sensible choice and keep the others for rooms where dust is not a health concern.

The HEPA upright has a two-speed roll, the XL a high-speed roll with automatic height and the second Professional a double helix roll. The roll sets how it handles carpet and hard floor. Choose by your floors: a controllable two-speed roll for a home with wood and carpet, an automatic height head for a mixed office and a spiral roll for carpet-heavy rooms, and remember that a faster roll lifts more but also wears belts and fringe more quickly.

The Commercial XL, LEED and Professional models are sold as commercial. They are simple and tough for their weight, but they have fewer features than the HEPA home model. The LEED version matters only in a certified building, so if that is not your situation, treat the plain Commercial XL as the same machine and spend the difference on spare belts and bags, which will do more for the machine's usefulness than a certificate on the box.

All models are belt-driven. A fast roll wears belts quickly, so replace them every six to twelve months and keep spares. A snapped belt is the commonest reason these machines stop cleaning, and the repair takes minutes, so it is the first thing to check whenever the roll stops, ahead of the motor, the bag and the hose, which are rarely at fault when the symptom is a roll that no longer turns.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filtration
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for HEPA media and for any statement about a sealed bag housing. The HEPA upright is the only model in the lineup that lists HEPA, and even there we treated the claim as a feature of the filter, not a guarantee about the whole machine.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and build
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted that all weigh about nine pounds and have thin frames, which is an advantage for carrying and a limit for durability, so we favored models whose listings describe a commercial build and whose parts, such as belts and bags, are easy to find.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brush control
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the two-speed, high-speed and double helix rolls, asking how each handles carpet, hard floor and fringe, and we gave the HEPA upright's controllable roll the most credit because the operator can match it to the floor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed belts and bags as the recurring costs.

cards.label: Home model
cards.text: The HEPA upright adds HEPA media and a two-speed roll. It suits a home with allergies.

cards.label: Commercial models
cards.text: The XL, LEED and Professional models are simple and light. They suit offices and homes that want a basic machine.

howToChoose.note: Choose HEPA for allergies, commercial for simplicity. A household that wants both should compare the bag cost and the filter schedule of the HEPA model with the lower running cost of the commercial ones before deciding.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A weight near nine pounds, a bag that does not weigh it down and a handle you can hold comfortably.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: All models weigh about nine pounds, so the choice is about features. The HEPA upright adds capacity with a large bag, while the commercial models keep the bag smaller and the body simpler for faster handling on stairs.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have allergies. The HEPA upright's media and roll control pay back.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need a basic light machine. The Professional or XL does the job.

maintenance.why: A packed bag collapses airflow and makes the motor work harder. Change it when it is about two thirds full, and seat the new bag flat against the intake so no gap lets dust bypass it.
A worn belt stops the roll and the machine then pushes dirt instead of lifting it. Keep a spare, and fit it untwisted around the motor shaft and the roll before you refit the cover.
Thread and hair bind the roll and strain the belt. Cut them free with scissors or a seam ripper, and spin the roll by hand afterward to confirm it turns freely.
A loaded filter strains the motor.

faq.a: The HEPA upright is best for a home with allergies, because it adds HEPA media and a controllable roll. The Commercial XL is the value workhorse, and the same machine in other trims serves offices that need compliance or a spiral roll.
About nine pounds, which is the brand's selling point.

faq.q: Are they good on thick carpet?
faq.a: Light machines work best on low and medium pile. Thick carpet favors heavier uprights, because weight presses the head into the pile and helps the roll agitate deeply, and a very light machine can skim the surface of a shag rug while looking busy and leaving the embedded dirt in place.

Yes, all of them. Keep spare bags and buy the style listed for your exact model, since a loose or misshapen bag lets dust past the filter and into the motor, and change the bag before it is completely full.

faq.q: How often do belts need changing?
faq.a: Every six to twelve months, or when the roll stops turning.

It means the machine meets criteria in a green building rating system. It does not change cleaning performance, so buy it only if a building specification asks for it, and otherwise choose on weight, bag and brush roll like any other light upright.
